samples.xml_description:
<module id="asyn_fifo">
    <description>Implement an asynchronous FIFO, FIFO bit width and depth can be configured(parameter DEPTH = 16, parameter WIDTH = 8).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="wclk">Write clock signal used for synchronous write operations.</input>
        <input id="rclk">Read clock signal used for synchronous read operations.</input>
        <input id="wrstn">Write reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="rrstn">Read reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="winc">Write increment signal. Used to trigger write operations.</input>
        <input id="rinc">Read increment signal. Used to trigger read operations.</input>
        <input id="wdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Write data input. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data to be written into the FIFO.</input>
        <output id="wfull">Write full signal. Indicates if the FIFO is full and cannot accept further write operations.</output>
        <output id="rempty">Read empty signal. Indicates if the FIFO is empty and cannot provide any data for read operations.</output>
        <output id="rdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Read data output. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data read from the FIFO.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH" value="8">FIFO bit width configuration parameter. Default value is 8.</parameter>
        <parameter id="DEPTH" value="16">FIFO depth configuration parameter. Default value is 16.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <wire id="wen" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Wire representing the write enable signal for the dual-port RAM.</wire>
        <wire id="ren" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Wire representing the read enable signal for the dual-port RAM.</wire>
        <reg id="waddr" width_description="$clog2(DEPTH)">Register storing the write address for the dual-port RAM.</reg>
        <reg id="raddr" width_description="$clog2(DEPTH)">Register storing the read address for the dual-port RAM.</reg>
        
        // Convert write pointer to Gray code
        <assign wptr[0] = waddr[0];
        <assign wptr[1] = waddr[1] ^ waddr[0];
        <assign wptr[2] = waddr[2] ^ waddr[1];
        <assign wptr[3] = waddr[3] ^ waddr[2]; 
        
        // Convert read pointer to Gray code
        <assign rptr[0] = raddr[0];
        <assign rptr[1] = raddr[1] ^ raddr[0];
        <assign rptr[2] = raddr[2] ^ raddr[1];
        <assign rptr[3] = raddr[3] ^ raddr[2];
        <always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn)> begin
            if(~wrstn) begin
                waddr <= 'b0;
            end else begin
                if(winc && !wfull) begin
                    waddr <= waddr + 1'b1;
                end
            end
        end
        
        <always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn)> begin
            if(~rrstn) begin
                raddr <= 'b0;
            end else begin
                if(rinc && !rempty) begin
                    raddr <= raddr + 1'b1;
                end
            end
        end
        <assign wen = winc & ~wfull;
        <assign ren = rinc & ~rempty;
        <assign rdata = ram.rdata;
        <assign waddr_bin = {wptr[3], wptr[3]^wptr[2], wptr[2]^wptr[1], wptr[1]^wptr[0]};
        <assign raddr_bin = {rptr[3], rptr[3]^rptr[2], rptr[2]^rptr[1], rptr[1]^rptr[0]};
        <assign wfull = (wptr == {~rptr[3], rptr[2:0]});
        <assign rempty = (rptr == wptr);
        <assign rdata = ram.rdata;
    </logic_description>
    
    <task>
        <step id="1">Create an instance of dual-port RAM, implementing a FIFO with configurable bit width and depth.</step>
        <step id="2">Instantiate the dual-port RAM module, connecting its ports to the corresponding ports of the FIFO module.</step>
        <step id="3">Develop logic for managing write and read addresses in the FIFO.</step>
        <step id="4">Implement a mechanism for converting binary pointers to Gray code.</step>
        <step id="5">Manage read and write operations, ensuring proper synchronization between the two pointers.</step>
        <step id="6">Generate full and empty signals based on comparisons between write and read pointers.</step>
        <step id="7">Connect input and output signals to the dual-port RAM module.</step>
        <step id="8">Test the functionality of the FIFO module through simulation.</step>
    </task>
    <implementation>
        // TODO: Implement this module here
        // Do not modify input and output pin definitions
        // You may create your own wires/regs, but do not change the name attribute of existing elements
        // Your implementation should start after this line, up to the next <task></task> block
        // Delete the following lines once you have implemented this module
        // Create an instance of dual-port RAM
        <dual_port_RAM id="ram"
                       DEPTH={DEPTH}
                       WIDTH={WIDTH}>
            <clock id="wclk"/>       // Write clock signal
            <clock id="rclk"/>       // Read clock signal
            <reset id="wrstn"/>      // Write reset signal
            <reset id="rrstn"/>      // Read reset signal
            <enable_write id="wenc"/>     // Write enable signal
            <enable_read id="renc"/>     // Read enable signal
            <write_address id="waddr"/>  // Write address
            <read_address id="raddr"/>   // Read address
            <write_data id="wdata"/>     // Write data
            <read_data id="rdata"/>      // Read data
        </dual_port_RAM>
        // Instantiate dual-port RAM
        // Connect input ports
        <connect id="connect_wclk">
            <from id="wclk"/>
            <to id="wclk"/>
        </connect>
        <connect id="connect_rclk">
            <from id="rclk"/>
            <to id="rclk"/>
        </connect>
        <connect id="connect_wrstn">
            <from id="wrstn"/>
            <to id="wrstn"/>
        </connect>
        <connect id="connect_rrstn">
            <from id="rrstn"/>
            <to id="rrstn"/>
        </connect>
        // Connect output ports
        <connect id="connect_renc">
            <from id="renc"/>
            <to id="renc"/>
        </connect>
        <connect id="connect_wenc">
            <from id="wen"/>
            <to id="wenc"/>
        </connect>
        <connect id="connect_waddr">
            <from id="waddr_bin"/>
            <to id="waddr"/>
        </connect>
        <connect id="connect_raddr">
            <from id="raddr_bin"/>
            <to id="raddr"/>
        </connect>
        <connect id="connect_wdata">
            <from id="wdata"/>
            <to id="wdata"/>
        </connect>
        <connect id="connect_rdata">
            <from id="rdata"/>
            <to id="rdata"/>
        </connect>
        // Develop logic for managing write and read addresses in the FIFO
        <always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn)> begin
            if(~wrstn) begin
                waddr <= 'b0;
            end else begin
                if(winc && !wfull) begin
                    waddr <= waddr + 1'b1;
                end
            end
        end
        <always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn)> begin
            if(~rrstn) begin
                raddr <= 'b0;
            end else begin
                if(rinc && !rempty) begin
                    raddr <= raddr + 1'b1;
                end
            end
        end
        // Implement a mechanism for converting binary pointers to Gray code
        <assign wen = winc & ~wfull;
        <assign ren = rinc & ~rempty;
        <assign rdata = ram.rdata;
        <assign waddr_bin = {wptr[3], wptr[3]^wptr[2], wptr[2]^wptr[1], wptr[1]^wptr[0]};
        <assign raddr_bin = {rptr[3], rptr[3]^rptr[2], rptr[2]^rptr[1], rptr[1]^rptr[0]};
        <assign wfull = (wptr == {~rptr[3], rptr[2:0]});
        <assign rempty = (rptr == wptr);
        <assign rdata = ram.rdata;
        // Manage read and write operations, ensuring proper synchronization between the two pointers
        // Generate full and empty signals based on comparisons between write and read pointers
        // Connect input and output signals to the dual-port RAM module
        // Test the functionality of the FIFO module through simulation
    endtask
    // Your implementation should end before this line, up to the next <task></task> block
</module>
